newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy unlikely to speed up soon -- BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy unlikely to speed up soon -- BOJ.

text.p: The recovery in Japan's economy is not likely to accelerate soon, given small and medium-sized firms' cautiousness about their production and employment, Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Wednesday.
He was speaking at a news conference following a two-day conference of BOJ branch managers which ended on Tuesday.
"Japan's economy is continuing to gradually recover. I have heard reports (from the BOJ branch managers) that they have felt firmness in recent economic recovery," Matsushita said.

"However, they also said the recovery movements are unlikely to accelerate at the moment, as small and medium-sized firms are retaining their cautiousness concerning production and employment," he said.

"For the economy to move on to a solid, self-sustained recovery track, it is important for a favourable economic cyclical mechanism, centering on private-sector demand, to strengthen further," he also said.
Market expectations that Japanese interest rates will go up in the future have receded recently, Matsushita also said.
He said the yield on the 10-year cash government bond had recently fallen to the 2.7 percent level from the 3.3 percent level it was at in mid-July.
But he added that it was inappropriate for the central bank to comment on specific interest rate levels.
"The market basically fluctuates from day to day due to various factors," he said.
Matsushita also said, however, that the central bank would continue to watch market movements as they reflected participants' views on the economy.

Referring to the BOJ's monetary policy, Matsushita said: "For the time being, it is appropriate for us to keep the emphasis on making the basis for an economic recovery more solid, and carefully watch developments in (economic) conditions."

Asked to comment on non-bank financial institution Nichiei Finance Co Ltd's filing for liquidation on Tuesday, Matsushita said such measures were sometimes an inevitable part of the procedure of coping with problem loans.
Financial institutions which have extended loans to non-bank institutions have already dealt with the situation by setting aside loan loss reserves, Matsushita said.
He stressed the importance of quickly dealing with problem loans to restore the health of the financial system and regain credibility at home and abroad.
"Dealing with non-banks with a long-term perspective in mind is not something that is going to have a negative impact. It is in line with restoring health in the system," he said.
